scope: Refresh primary-source comparison of open-source DWG/DXF implementations and downstream readers; derive implementation-readiness and validation refinements without inferring a local defect or promoting support claims.

method.kind: Primary project manuals, documentation, repository README/API pages, and current consumer build configuration
method.sourcePinning: The reviewed public master/stable pages are mutable; no peer commit hash, binary hash, or exact local build was established. Any runtime comparison must pin these before execution.
method.evidenceRule: Published route/version matrices, aggregate coverage figures, opaque retention, projected output, and self-round-trip are not per-feature semantic proof. Each signal is scoped to the peer and documented route only.

evidence.topic: LibreDWG class stability, route/version limits, and fuzz lanes
evidence.observed: The manual classifies objects as stable, unstable, debugging, or unhandled; describes unknown/proxy-like conversion and same-version unknown-bit preservation conditions; and documents fuzzing routes for DWG, ASCII/binary DXF, JSON, and converter modes. Aggregate coverage language coexists with class, direction, version, and writer limits.
doesNotEstablish: uniform semantic support for every class or version
safe arbitrary editing/re-encoding of unsupported classes
that a same-version unknown-blob path supports cross-version conversion
that fuzz capability means the local implementation has equivalent coverage
evidence.planUse: Keep read/write/conversion and class status separate. Compare output object class and source-handle disposition; require loss reporting. Run broad fuzzing at scheduled security checkpoints rather than every leaf slice.

evidence.topic: ACadSharp published version matrix versus per-feature evidence
evidence.observed: The project advertises DxfReader/DxfWriter/DwgReader/DwgWriter routes by AC version and exposes a typed document/API model.
doesNotEstablish: per-entity or per-field fidelity in all listed routes
complete graph, owner, handle, and reference preservation
successful acceptance by unrelated native CAD applications
the exact tested revision, because the referenced public pages are mutable
evidence.planUse: Use the version matrix to select candidate route/version probes only. Pin a release/commit and add exact feature-level assertions, warning capture, graph checks, and output-consumer evidence before using it as a differential.

evidence.topic: ezdxf opaque storage, copy/edit boundaries, and ACIS subset
evidence.observed: Unsupported DXF entities can be stored as tag-storage records for export, while xref/copy excludes ACAD_TABLE and unknown tag-storage entities. The ACIS docs describe a limited parser; unsupported content can load as NONE_ENTITY and be lost on export.
doesNotEstablish: typed/editable support merely because original tags can be re-emitted
graph-aware cross-document copy of all opaque entities
evidence.planUse: Test same-document opaque pass-through separately from typed edit/write, xref/copy, and ACIS interpretation. Assert exact raw bytes/tags only on an explicitly supported route and report unsupported operations.

evidence.topic: GDAL/OGR as projected geometry and raw-carrier comparator
evidence.observed: The DXF driver projects supported records to OGR features, offers optional raw unhandled group-code values, documents OCS limitations for selected entities, skips ACIS/ASM solid geometry by default, and can expose raw ASM plus an affine transform in extensible mode for AC1027+ DXF. Current docs say binary DXF reading starts in GDAL 3.12.
doesNotEstablish: DWG parsing or complete CAD document/object graph preservation
binary-DXF semantic parity with ASCII input for every entity
that ASM payload plus transform has been associated with the correct source entity
evidence.planUse: Use GDAL only as a pinned optional geometry-projection/raw-carrier comparator with explicit driver version/options. Keep raw payload, entity association, transform, ACIS parse, B-rep and native acceptance separate. Include binary-DXF syntax in its eligible route matrix, not as a new support claim.

evidence.topic: LibreCAD fast/slow test architecture as a consumer compatibility model
evidence.observed: Current LibreCAD build configuration groups fast and slow test sources, offers per-test executables, and gates cross-read smoke separately from full application tests. LibreCAD consumes a bundled libdxfrw fork, so this is a consumer integration path and not an independent parser vote.
doesNotEstablish: that a passing consumer build exercises this upstream checkout
runtime behavior of every importer/writer option
semantic support from API or source compatibility alone
evidence.planUse: Keep strict affected-target plus focused-test checks per slice; schedule full/family suites, cross-read, and native GUI/runtime checks at composed gates. Label whether a compatibility test links the fork or upstream source.

capabilityMatrixFields: raw/opaque payload and hash when applicable
differentialProtocol: pin peer release/commit, build flags, executable hash, and option set
use locally authored/runtime-generated controls or eligible repository-owned samples
compare source-handle/owner/class disposition and graph edges, not only entity totals
capture peer warnings, exit status, output version/hash, and independent consumer outcome
treat peer self-round-trip as codec consistency only
implementationReadiness.validationCadence: Per implementation slice: touched strict build, one focused existing fast test, relevant compile/API compatibility check, git diff --check. At composed checkpoints: family/full suites, sanitizers/fuzzing, pinned peer differentials, and native CAD/shape consumers.
implementationReadiness.lineagePolicy: Count related ports and downstream applications of the same parser lineage once; use each tool only for its documented evidence layer.
